content.overview: BNS s. 66 — Punishment for causing death or resulting in persistent vegetative state of victim.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Punishment for causing death or resulting in persistent vegetative state of victim. BNS restatement of IPC 376A. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 376A. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 66 is the rule on “Punishment for causing death or resulting in persistent vegetative state of victim”. The section provides that whoever, commits an offence punishable under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) of section 64 and in the course of such commission inflicts an injury which causes the death of the woman or causes the woman to be in a persistent vegetative state, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, or with death. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 66 exists so that “Punishment for causing death or resulting in persistent vegetative state of victim” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail

Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 66 (Punishment for causing death or resulting in persistent vegetative state of victim), Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever, commits an offence punishable under sub-section
   (2) (2) of section 64 and in the course of such commission inflicts an injury which causes the death of the woman or causes the woman to be in a persistent vegetative state, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, or with death
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 66 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 66 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

learningObjectives: Understand the severe penalty under BNS s. 66 for catastrophic injuries during rape.
Analyze the twin outcomes: causing death of the victim, or causing persistent vegetative state.
Identify the sentencing options: minimum 20 years RI to natural life, or death.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 66 provides that whoever commits an offence punishable under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) of section 64 and in the course of such commission inflicts an injury which causes the death of the woman or causes the woman to be in a persistent vegetative state, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, or with death.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Brutal sexual assaults that cause fatal injuries or reduce the victim to an irreversible persistent vegetative state constitute the most heinous form of aggravated sexual homicide, punishable with natural life or death.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 66 (corresponding to IPC s. 376A).
Prerequisite: Commission of rape under s. 64.
Contemporaneous act: Inflicting an injury in the course of such commission.
Consequence 1: Causes the death of the woman.
Consequence 2: Causes the woman to be in a persistent vegetative state (PVS).
Penalty: RI minimum twenty years extending to natural life, OR DEATH.
essentialIngredients: The accused committed rape under s. 64.
In the course of the rape, the accused inflicted bodily injury on the victim.
The injury caused the death of the victim, OR reduced her to a persistent vegetative state.
Sentence: Minimum 20 years RI up to natural life, or death.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 66 addresses extreme brutality during sexual assault (often referred to as the post-Nirbhaya provision). It does not require proof of premeditated intent to murder; it applies whenever, in the course of rape, the assailant inflicts injuries that result in death or an irreversible vegetative state (where brain stem functions continue but cerebral cognitive function is permanently lost). Because the physical brutality directly destroys human life or consciousness, the law empowers the court to impose capital punishment or life imprisonment for the offender's natural life.
examples: Teaching example (Fatal internal injuries): An assailant inflicts massive internal blunt force trauma during rape, resulting in hemorrhagic shock and death. Section 66 applies; the assailant is liable to death or natural life imprisonment.

Teaching example (Persistent vegetative state): An assailant strangles a victim during rape, depriving her brain of oxygen for eight minutes. The victim survives on life support in an irreversible coma with permanent loss of higher brain function. Section 66 directly applies.
distinctions: Section 66 vs Section 103 (Murder): Under s. 66, causation of death in the course of rape triggers capital punishment without needing separate proof of independent murderous intention.
Persistent Vegetative State: A defined medical condition of permanent cognitive unresponsiveness certified by medical boards.
problemApplication: Issue: What is the liability of an assailant who brutally assaulted a victim during rape, resulting in massive brain damage leaving her in a permanent coma?
Rule: Under BNS s. 66, inflicting injury in the course of rape causing a persistent vegetative state carries twenty years RI up to natural life, or death.
Application: Medical board reports certify irreversible persistent vegetative state caused by traumatic brain injury during the assault.
Conclusion: The assailant is convicted under s. 66 and faces natural life imprisonment or death.
